title: Declare the gate contract in the breakdown analysis schema
description:
The analysis-agent JSON contract (`.claude/skills/jit-breakdown/references/plan-schema.md`) declares `gate_tier` but no `gates` field. In practice the orchestrator needs the concrete gate list per child at creation time, so each run re-invents the field ad hoc in the dispatch prompt. During the 2821e177 story recursion, six independently dispatched agents produced drifting shapes (some emitted `gates`, one emitted only `gate_tier`), and the creation script crashed mid-run on the missing key, leaving partially created state that had to be recovered by hand-reconstructing ref-to-UUID maps.

Make the schema the single contract: `plan-schema.md` declares both `gate_tier` (the named tier) and `gates` (the concrete gate-key array for that tier, required, non-empty for implementation children), and the analysis prompt template points at the schema instead of restating it. The executing skill treats a child missing the field as a schema-validation failure before any issue is created, so drift surfaces as a parse error rather than a mid-creation crash.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `plan-schema.md` declares `gate_tier` and a required `gates` array per child issue, with the tier-to-gates mapping supplied by the orchestrator as dispatch input.
- [hard] REQ-02: the analysis prompt template references the schema for the gate fields rather than defining them inline.
- [hard] REQ-03: jit-breakdown validates every returned child against the schema (all required fields present, `gates` non-empty where the tier demands it) before creating any issue, and reports a schema violation without writing partial state.
